captions.caption: A warning sign with a skull and crossbones reads "DANGER MINES".
The "DANGER MINES" sign is displayed against a dark background.
The skull and crossbones graphic is shown on the mine warning sign.
The "DANGER MINES" sign remains on screen before the scene changes.
A large grey military aircraft is parked on a runway under a cloudy sky.
The front of the KC-10 Extender tanker aircraft is shown on the tarmac.
A staircase is positioned next to the parked military tanker aircraft.
The nose and cockpit of the grey aircraft are visible on the airfield.
The tanker aircraft sits stationary on the runway as the camera angle shifts.
A view from directly underneath the tail of the aircraft shows the refueling boom.
The "60th AMW" text is visible on the tail section of the tanker.
The refueling boom is retracted under the tail of the stationary aircraft.
The underside of the aircraft's tail and its refueling equipment are shown.
A low-angle shot captures the rear engines and tail of the KC-10 Extender.
The tanker's refueling boom is positioned at the back of the fuselage.
The tail section of the grey military aircraft is framed against the sky.
The aircraft's rear engines and refueling boom are visible from the ground.
The camera focuses on the tail and refueling apparatus of the tanker.
The tail of the aircraft is shown with mountains in the far distance.
Another military aircraft is seen parked in the background on the tarmac.
The tail section and horizontal stabilizers of the tanker are shown.
The refueling boom hangs from the back of the parked KC-10 Extender.
The camera pans across the rear of the aircraft on the airfield.
An F/A-18 fighter jet flies in formation behind a refueling tanker.
The fighter jet's refueling probe is extended as it approaches the tanker.
Multiple F/A-18 jets are visible flying through the clouds in formation.
The refueling basket is deployed from the tanker for the approaching jet.
The pilot of the F/A-18 maneuvers the jet toward the refueling drogue.
The fighter jet's probe nears the center of the refueling basket.
The jet makes contact with the refueling equipment in mid-air.
The F/A-18 is connected to the tanker's refueling line above the clouds.
The aircraft fly steadily together during the refueling process.
A close-up view shows the connection between the jet and the drogue.
The fighter jet maintains its position as it receives fuel from the tanker.
Other fighter jets follow closely behind in the refueling formation.
The pilot in the cockpit of the F/A-18 is visible during the flight.
The tanker and fighter jet continue their mission over a cloud layer.
The refueling hose stays extended between the two military aircraft.
The jet makes minor adjustments to stay aligned with the tanker.
The refueling operation is seen from the perspective of the tanker's boom operator.
The fighter jet remains connected to the basket as they fly through the sky.
An F/A-18 jet is seen flying close to the refueling basket above the clouds.
The jet's refueling probe is aimed at the center of the drogue.
The aircraft fly through a bright, cloudy sky during the refueling mission.
The F/A-18 maneuvers to maintain a stable connection with the tanker.
The refueling probe is firmly locked into the basket of the tanker.
The jet continues to receive fuel while flying in formation.
A close-up shot focuses on the refueling probe entering the drogue.
The connection between the fighter jet and the tanker is highlighted.
The pilot is visible through the canopy of the F/A-18 during refueling.
The aircraft fly over a dense layer of white clouds in the sunlight.
The refueling process continues with the jet following the tanker's lead.
An F/A-18 jet is shown connected to the refueling line from a distance.
The jet banks slightly while remaining attached to the refueling basket.
The tanker and fighter jet are framed against a vast expanse of clouds.
The pilot maneuvers the aircraft to stay in the refueling position.
The F/A-18 follows the tanker steadily through the upper atmosphere.
The refueling probe is visible as it stays connected to the drogue.
The jet begins to slowly disconnect from the refueling equipment.
The F/A-18 pulls its refueling probe away from the basket.
